note: Generic job assumptions for kit/cloudcost.py. Hours are assumptions with stated bases, not measurements. GPU containers are assumed to request 4 physical cores (8 vCPU) and 32 GiB memory unless stated; Modal bills CPU and memory on top of the GPU.

2p5d_9um.description: 2.5D reader at about 9 um (e.g. public ink_9um hybrid 3D-2D checkpoints, Hecate 9.6 um)
2p5d_9um.basis: Measured on an Apple M1 Pro (MPS): ink_9um, both directions, all of w045 in 649 to 679 s per seed (docs/mac.md) over a 40.0 cm2 map (docs/logs/2026-10-07-novel-checks.md), about 8 s per cm2 per pass. High assumes no GPU speedup over that; typical and low assume 3x and 8x (unverified). 28 slices as in the official 9 um render (https://scrollprize.org/tutorial5).

2p5d_2um.description: 2.5D reader at 2.4 um (e.g. organiser 2 um canonical model, PHerc. 1667 iteration models, Hecate 2.4 um)
2p5d_2um.basis: Official tutorial: 2.5D inference on a full segment takes on the order of an hour on a single GPU (https://scrollprize.org/tutorial5). The tutorial segment's published 2.4 um prediction is 51,960 x 31,960 px, 95.6 cm2 of canvas (TIFF header of the public prediction file linked from the tutorial), so about 38 s per cm2 of canvas or more per surface cm2. High covers test-time mirroring or a slower card. GPU type in the tutorial is not stated.

3d_l2.description: Native 3D reader at pyramid level 2 of a 2.4 um scan (9.6 um voxels), e.g. villa full_3d_single_wrap
3d_l2.basis: Official tutorial: about 78,000 patches and about 2.5 h on an H100 for the tutorial segment (https://scrollprize.org/tutorial5); 9,000 s over 95.6 cm2 of canvas is about 94 s per cm2. Staging uses an 80-voxel band (the tutorial patch depth); chunk-aligned reads fetch more.

3d_2um.description: Native 3D reader at full 2.4 um resolution (e.g. full_3d at level 0; mesh-free 3D readers such as ink_3d_dino_guided are assumed similar or heavier)
3d_2um.basis: Interpretation: the tutorial says full resolution plans hundreds of thousands of patches against about 78,000 at level 2, so 3x to 16x the level-2 time per cm2 (about 95 s). Not measured; time one patch batch before any run.
